Country.evidence_source: After receiving IRB approval from The Ohio State University, participants from a regional campus were recruited from introductory and upper-level psychology classes during three academic terms.

Sample.evidence_source: From the initial data set of 749 participants, 675 (367 women and 308 men) remained, and their data were analyzed. Test–retest data from 208 participants (135 women and 73 men) were gathered.

Survey method.evidence_source: Interested students signed up on the psychology department's research management website and, from there, clicked a link to a webpage that hosted the informed consent sheet. Upon providing consent, participants were directed to the survey webpage.

Percent of white in participants.evidence_source: They ranged in age from 18 to 56 (Mage = 20.34, SD = 5.08) and identified as White (79.1%), African American (11.0%), Asian American (4.1%), Latina/Latino (0.7%), Native American (0.3%), or multiracial (4.6%). They identified as White (81.3%), African American (8.6%), Asian American (3.4%), Latino/Latina (0.5%), Native American (0.5%), or multiracial (5.8%).

Mean age of participants.evidence_source: They ranged in age from 18 to 56 (Mage = 20.34, SD = 5.08). They ranged in age from 18 to 47 (Mage = 20.27, SD = 4.53).

Percentage of college or higher of parti.evidence_source: They were first-year college students (76.7%), sophomores (17.2%), juniors (3.7%), or seniors (1.9%); three participants (0.4%) did not report their college status. They were first-year students (76.5%), sophomores (16.8%), juniors (4.3%), and seniors (1.9%). Calculation: For the first sample, 76.7 + 17.2 + 3.7 + 1.9 = 99.5%. For the second sample, 76.5 + 16.8 + 4.3 + 1.9 = 99.5%.

Mean BMI of participants.evidence_source: Average body mass index (BMI) was 24.21 (SD = 5.56) for women and 25.02 (SD = 5.27) for men.

Source of sample.evidence_source: participants from a regional campus were recruited from introductory and upper-level psychology classes during three academic terms.

Assessment of BA.evidence_source: Participants were not informed that they would be taking the BAS-2 again or that the purpose of the study was to gauge the stability of the BAS-2. The 19 items in the BAS-2 item pool were administered.

Assessment of BMI.evidence_source: Participants reported their height in feet and inches and weight in pounds, which we used to calculate BMI: (weight × 703)/height in inches2.

Number of studies.evidence_source: This study was described as an investigation of body attitudes, eating habits, and well-being among college students. All students received research credit for their participation, and after finishing this survey, were invited to participate in "a 3-week follow-up study on body attitudes" for additional research credit. This indicates one study with two data collection points/sub-samples.

section_summary.extract_value: This section details the methodology of a study conducted at The Ohio State University. It describes the recruitment of college students via an online survey, data screening procedures, and demographic characteristics of two sample subsets: an initial sample of 675 participants (367 women, 308 men) and a 3-week follow-up sample of 208 participants (135 women, 73 men). The section also outlines the various measures used, including the BAS-2 for body appreciation and self-reported height and weight for BMI calculation.
